title: One model per family on a zero-padded unified feature vector, encoded twice (Python and JS)
context: encode_design_unified() in train_synth.py and SynthEncoding.encode() in 10-encoding.js build the same fixed-length vector: mode one-hot, then term and factor slots padded to max_terms / max_factors. The layout is read from the bundle's encoding block, but the encoding logic itself exists in both languages and must change together (CLAUDE.md).

options.name: Unified vector, mirrored by hand (current)
options.summary: One family model; Python and JS encoders kept slot-for-slot identical, checked by tests/roundtrip.js.
pros: Bundle-driven layout tolerates a larger term cap without page edits
cons: Two implementations to keep in lockstep
New modes or fields (per-axis cell scale, surface_b) need both sides and a retrain

options.name: Encoding spec as data, both sides generated
options.summary: Describe slots declaratively in the bundle (or a shared JSON) and have thin interpreters in Python and JS.
pros: Adding a field becomes one edit
Drift becomes impossible rather than tested-for
cons: Interpreter must cover term structure, which is not flat

options.name: Per-mode or per-preset models
options.summary: Separate models per mode or per preset family.

recommendation: README "Unified feature vector" states the choice and its trade-off; CLAUDE.md requires the two encoders to change together; tests/roundtrip.js checks 600/600 seeds re-encode exactly.
strain: Two known encoder gaps (Sweep's per-axis cell_scale_x/y/z and field-pair PI-TPMS surface_b) are waiting on a coordinated Python + JS + retrain change (docs/NEXT-UP.md).
